newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia needs to develop faster - PM Mahathir.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia needs to develop faster - PM Mahathir.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamed said on Monday Malaysia has to develop faster in order to boost its people's living standards and narrow the gap with developed countries, the Bernama news agency reported.

"We have to move fast and run faster. If we were to run slower, we will never catch up and the gap would be even greater and forever, we will be left behind," the national news agency quoted Mahathir as saying at a function in eastern Sarawak state.
Mahathir was responding to criticisms that the country's growth was too rapid and its economy was overheating.
"It is not over-heating, it is well-planned development," he said.
Malaysia has logged an average Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of eight percent for the past decade. Mahathir said on Friday that GDP growth of 8.0 percent for 1997 was achievable.

But last week, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia may defer some big import items and less important infrastructure projects to cushion the impact of a weak ringgit on the trade account.
The Malaysian currency has fallen almost 12 percent against the dollar in the last month.
Mahathir said on Monday the government was aiming the development projects at improving its citizens' living standards.
"We are prepared to work hard to enrich the country for the better life of the people," he said.
